findings.text: Guest visible identifier writes are validated field by field against a reset limit. Registers seen as zero accept only zero, registers without feature metadata are rejected, fully writable fields must equal the safe combination of requested and limit values, and unwritable bits must match the limit.

For debug and performance fields the safe comparison uses lower is safer semantics, covering AArch64 debug version plus PMU version and the AArch32 performance monitor field, independent of host descriptor type.

Sanitised identifier reads yield zero when zero visibility applies, otherwise start from host sanitised state, apply per register sanitisation for debug plus processor plus instruction set plus memory model identifiers, then apply nested limits when that vcpu capability is enabled.

Instruction set sanitisation gates authentication fields on vcpu support, gates timer wait behavior on platform capability plus healthy counter offset, restricts newer registers to small allowlists, and memory model sanitisation clears index plus virtualization indicators while gating overlay permission on system support.

First processor feature sanitisation hides vector support without vcpu support, unconditionally hides activity monitor plus partitioning support, advertises interrupt support when the host has it, and forces speculation indicators toward unaffected when host reports unaffected.

Second processor feature sanitisation hides tagging without VM support and clears matrix plus random trap plus interrupt plus guard plus hardening plus extended tagging plus fault address plus partitioning fraction indicators, while fault fraction survives only with platform extension plus host RAS support.

Third processor feature sanitisation keeps only a small floating plus tagging set, drops tagging indicators without VM tagging support, and advertises guest interrupt capability when host global interrupt state reports version five.

Debug sanitisation caps debug version at a recent level, synthesizes PMU version from a global limit only when the vcpu has a PMU, hides profiling plus branch record indicators, and AArch32 performance values derive from AArch64 values with defined mappings for older encodings.

Vector identifier visibility is zero without vcpu vector support, AArch32 identifiers are zero plus user write ignored without 32 bit support, one helper always reports zero, and vector plus matrix plus floating extension registers are hidden unless the matching capability is present.

Several setters accept historic values once exposed and normalize them before generic validation, including older PMU encodings moved toward not implemented, echoed partitioning plus deprecated virtualization fields ignored when matching host, and legacy tagging fraction restored toward host.

Undersized debug and coprocessor debug values plus intermediate AArch32 performance values plus disabled required execution levels plus mismatched stage two granule support with nesting plus reserved cache encodings are rejected without storing.

VM identifier registers move from mutable to immutable at first run. Before start writes are validated and stored and reads use locking. After start reads avoid locking and writes succeed only when equal to stored state.

The VM architecture configuration mutex serializes identifier store plus pre start load, is held across validation plus store and across pre start load, is released on early busy return and normal completion, and is not taken for post start loads nor for zero and ignore helpers.

Guest traps for identifier plus cache topology registers reject writes to read only views, return VM stored values for identifier plus cache type and vcpu stored values for cache level, pass through cache select state, and derive cache size state from masked select when in range.

Cache level reset synthesizes level count plus sharing levels plus per level kinds from host coherence requirements, adds tag type at the top when VM tagging is enabled, stores the result in vcpu state and returns it, while explicit writes reject reserved bits plus incoherent empty topology.

Tagging and nested registers are hidden unless the matching VM or vcpu capability is present, tagging descriptors use undefined access with unknown reset plus per register storage and tagging visibility, and misdirected nested control traps are reported as bad traps.

Internal oversize status from feature validation is mapped to invalid argument for the one register interface, while several setters silently rewrite accepted legacy encodings before storage so observed values can differ from supplied values without error.

Zero visibility still permits a read path yielding zero and for AArch32 also permits ignored user writes, whereas hidden visibility removes the register from view, so confusing them changes observability and writability.
After first run a mismatched identifier write reports busy, unknown cache encodings report missing entry, and invalid feature combinations report invalid argument after internal oversize mapping.
External mutual exclusion primitive used to serialize identifier configuration; implementation owned elsewhere.
External bitfield extraction helper used to test execution state enablement in processor feature writes; implementation owned elsewhere.
